title: Quenched Algerian Dates Tagine
description: A sweet and sour North African dish featuring dates, cocoa powder, and tempered chocolate. Perfect for adventurous eaters looking for a unique dessert.
instructions: In a medium saucepan, combine the dates, water, cinnamon, and ginger. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a separate saucepan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the flour and whisk to combine. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually add the sugar to the saucepan with the flour mixture and whisk to combine. Cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the cocoa powder to the saucepan and whisk to combine. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Remove the date mixture from the heat and stir in the tempered chocolate until melted and smooth.
Strain the date mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan, pressing the solids to extract the liquid.
Add the flour mixture to the date mixture and whisk to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5-7 minutes, or until thickened.
Stir in the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter until melted.
Pour the mixture into individual serving cups or ramekins.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.
